1#main: How they carry out a large or small dead body, and with which bier. In it are 7 seifim. At first they would uncover the faces of the rich and cover the faces of the poor because they would blacken in a famine year and the poor would be ashamed while alive; they enacted that all faces be covered.
2#main: One does not place a Sefer Torah on the bier of a sage.
3#main: It is the honor of a sage to take him out through the doorway and not lower him through roofs; on the first bier and not switch from bier to bier.
4#main: A child of thirty days — they take him out in arms to the cemetery and not in a coffin, and he is buried by one woman and two men, but not one man and two women because of yichud; and they do not stand in a row for him nor say over him the mourners' blessing and condolences, even if we know his months were complete.
5#main: A child of thirty full days goes out in a gloskema (meaning: coffin; Targum: and place him in a coffin — Nimmukei Yosef) carried on side-poles (meaning: wide board; meaning of side-poles: arms); and they stand in a row and say over him the mourners' blessing and condolences. A child of twelve months goes out on a bier; and all who go out on a bier — many accompany him; and one who does not go out on a bier — many do not accompany him; and whoever is known to the many — the many are occupied with him; and whoever is not known to the many — the many are not obligated to be occupied with him.
6#main: A child who died before being circumcised — they circumcise him at his grave without a blessing and give him a name.
7#main: One does not take out the dead on a bier unless his head and majority were intact.
